### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, touching **92** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 99364ea75b015b1d8391174a9ead5395977e7ecd`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 99364ea75b015b1d8391174a9ead5395977e7ecd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ff1eaf698cf7b2be4c1cd7c4a0c88db284b688d1` — the merge of head `faaa3a6d9a230d81d6d0f88ab64c7e91f224d000` into base `99364ea75b015b1d8391174a9ead5395977e7ecd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ff1eaf698cf7b2be4c1cd7c4a0c88db284b688d1 && git checkout ff1eaf698cf7b2be4c1cd7c4a0c88db284b688d1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 99364ea75b015b1d8391174a9ead5395977e7ecd faaa3a6d9a230d81d6d0f88ab64c7e91f224d000 && git checkout -B drift-repro 99364ea75b015b1d8391174a9ead5395977e7ecd && git merge --no-ff faaa3a6d9a230d81d6d0f88ab64c7e91f224d000

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 99364ea75b015b1d8391174a9ead5395977e7ecd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 99364ea75b015b1d8391174a9ead5395977e7ecd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** · #31395 · Head-sha: `2de7d355` · 2026-11-08T17:23Z · report 6724614823

- **Shape:** draft to `main`, first line `Fixes #31395` (the whole card is done: the LOWER/CONVERT route, docs stated). `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` at line start in the body and the changeset. 14 files, +447 / -32, all inside the claimed surface (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/`, the SQL Server section of `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`, one changeset). Not governed; under 3000 lines.
- **Premise measured:** live on SQL Server 2022 in the card container: a lower-case fragment went 0 → 1 row on `$contains` / `$startsWith` / `$endsWith` / `$like`, `$icontains` / `$ilike` match both cases, `nvarchar` controls identical. GUID columns are learned from `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS` (`primeMssqlGuidColumns`), never from the comparand.
- **Read in the diff:** the construct is three new functions after `mssqlAsciiLower` in `sql-driver-predicate-emitters.ts`, reached only when `guidColumn && dialectName === 'mssql'`; `textMatchPredicate` and `likePatternPredicate` are untouched, so #31394's move of the text-match table does not overlap. Every other dialect compiles as before.
- **Gates (report, head `2de7d355`):** 99 derived / 99 run / 0 unrun; eslint and typecheck exit 0; driver-sql full 246 files with the live cell, service-datasource 74, objectql 570; dogfood 440 passed / 3 skipped; conformance ledger 66 covered / 6 DEBT before and after; ablations A1–A5 and L1 red, then restored. PR check-runs: still running at this record; landing waits for every check green or expected skip.
- **Changeset and docs, sentence by sentence:** the changeset's two paragraphs and the docs' GUID bullet say the same thing the diff does (the operator list, the `LOWER(CONVERT(nvarchar(36), col))` form, the case-exact consequence, equality/`$in` unchanged, the catalog read).

**Open questions, ruled by the seat:**
1. Upper-case fragments on the case-exact operators: **A, keep.** The case-exact contract (#6518) is against the value a read answers, and SQL Server reads GUIDs lower-case. The upper-case answer never shipped: #31327's changeset (`.changeset/31327-mssql-federation-dialect.md`) is still pending release, so no released caller sees the change. The changeset states the move and the fix (`$icontains` / `$ilike`).
2. A failed catalog read stays silent: **A, keep**, the `primeMssqlPagingKey` precedent; the data read on the same connection fails loudly.
3. `$like` / `$ilike` in the same PR: **A, accept.** Same column-reading defect, same emitter, one flag; leaving them out would make two operators disagree on one column.

**Deviations accepted:** PR opened with no assignee (the seat assigns it); live cell is local only, CI runs the live cases as named skips; `test:repo` left to CI's Test Core.
**Out of scope:** none filed.
**Landing:** when every check on `2de7d355` is green or an expected skip, the seat readies it and arms auto-merge.

## 席位核对 · conflict round · head `faaa3a6d` · 2026-11-08T18:57Z

**Verdict: ACCEPT.**

- Context: the PR was removed from the merge queue at 18:36:57Z when #31625 (`90457e74`) landed on `main`. `main` (`cb7b3ccb`) is merged in as a merge commit; there was no rebase.
- The only conflict was the docblock above `textMatchPredicate`, and #31625's side is kept whole. `textMatchPredicate` and `likePatternPredicate` are byte-for-byte `main`'s.
- `main` had moved the mssql construct table to core, so the #31395 siblings now build on it instead of on the deleted local helpers:
  - `mssqlGuidTextMatch` calls `dialectTextMatchSql` (dialect `mssql`), with a column emitter of `LOWER(CONVERT(nvarchar(36), ??))`. It reuses core's escape, fold and `ESCAPE` binding, and copies nothing.
  - `mssqlGuidLikePattern` uses core's `mssqlCaseExactSql` / `mssqlAsciiLowerSql`.
  - `mssqlGuidText` is unchanged.
  - The `guidColumn` dispatch in `applyLike` / `applyLikePattern` is unchanged.
- The 19 compiled pins assert the exact SQL strings and stay green (driver-sql 4132 tests pass), so the emitted SQL is byte-identical to the head that passed the live mssql cell (`360a5df4`). The live cell is not re-run; the pins carry the identity.
- Earlier rulings (OQ1–OQ3) stand.

Landing: after CI is green on `faaa3a6d`, the seat re-arms `automerge_enable`.
